beats.say: Raw supplier files, product images, and logs. All piled together.
beats.label: In the pile

beats.say: Nobody can find anything. That is not a data lake. That is a data swamp.
beats.label: The problem
beats.head: A data swamp

beats.say: One idea turns it around: a lake is Cloud Storage, plus discipline.
beats.label: Station 3.3 · Using a data lake
beats.head: A lake = Cloud Storage + discipline

beats.say: Discipline has five parts. One: zones.
Data moves from raw, to staged, to curated. Each zone is cleaner than the last.
beats.label: Three zones

beats.say: Two: open formats, like Parquet, Avro and Iceberg. Any engine can read them.
beats.label: 2 · Open formats
beats.head: Parquet, Avro, Iceberg

check.prompt: Analysts may see only some columns of the files in a bucket. What do you give them?
options: A BigLake table with column security
check.why: A BigLake table gives row and column security. The analysts never get the bucket.

beats.say: Three: discovery. Dataplex finds the files, and registers them as tables.
beats.label: 3 · Discovery
beats.head: Dataplex turns files into tables

beats.say: Four: security. BigLake tables give row and column security over files.
beats.label: 4 · Security
beats.head: BigLake: row and column security on files

beats.say: So analysts query the table. They never get the whole bucket.
beats.label: Why it matters
beats.head: Query the table, not the bucket

beats.say: Five: cost. Lifecycle rules move old files to colder, cheaper classes.
beats.label: 5 · Cost
beats.head: Lifecycle rules keep it cheap

beats.say: The trap: giving analysts read access to the whole bucket, to hide a few columns.
beats.label: Exam trap
beats.text: Bucket-wide access when only some columns are allowed

beats.say: Zones. Open formats. Discovery. BigLake security. And lifecycle rules.
beats.label: Station 3.3
